chapters.title: Patient Denying Alcohol Problems
chapters.description: Explore the patient's perspective on drinking and build rapport without judgment.
chapters.briefing: Michael is attending an appointment about poor sleep and elevated blood pressure. He does not see his evening drinking as a concern. Your task is to understand his perspective and explore a next step together.
chapters.openingLine: I'm really just here because I haven't been sleeping well.
concerns: Pressure to change before he is ready
privateDisclosures: Usually drinks four to six beers in the evening
Worries about being tired at work
His partner has mentioned his drinking
chapters.empatheticReaction: Become more open when the learner asks permission and acknowledges that work and family matter to you.
chapters.judgmentalReaction: Become guarded if labeled or ordered to stop; explain that you still work and support your family.

objectives.text: Introduce yourself and establish rapport
Explain confidentiality and ask permission to discuss alcohol
Ask open-ended questions about drinking habits
Explore how drinking affects daily life
Identify concerns and acknowledge feelings
Explore readiness to consider change
Discuss risks and support options with permission
Collaboratively identify an appropriate next step
Close the conversation respectfully

chapters.title: Opioid Use and Treatment Resistance
chapters.description: Understand concerns about treatment while respecting the patient's autonomy.
chapters.briefing: Jordan has a history of opioid use and is reluctant to discuss treatment. Focus on trust, the patient's previous experiences, and what support they would be willing to consider.
chapters.openingLine: If this is another lecture about treatment, I've already heard it.
privateDisclosures: Taking time off work is difficult
Would consider hearing about flexible support if allowed to choose
chapters.empatheticReaction: Explain your previous experience when the learner listens without arguing and respects your choices.
chapters.judgmentalReaction: Withdraw when threatened or told there is only one acceptable choice.

objectives.text: Introduce yourself and establish trust
Ask permission to discuss opioid use and support
Explore previous experiences with treatment
Acknowledge concerns without arguing
Ask about practical barriers to support
Explore goals and readiness in the patient's own words
Ask permission before discussing support options
Agree on a patient-chosen next step
Summarize and close respectfully

chapters.title: Concerned Family Member
chapters.description: Acknowledge a parent's frustration while respecting an adult patient's privacy.
chapters.setting: Family conversation with the healthcare team
chapters.briefing: Pat is worried about their adult child's substance use and wants the team to fix the situation immediately. Practice empathy, clarify what can be discussed, and explore support without promising a particular outcome.
chapters.openingLine: Why can't someone just make my child get help?
privateDisclosures: Wants someone to explain what support is available for families
chapters.empatheticReaction: Express fear beneath the frustration when the learner acknowledges how difficult the situation feels.
chapters.judgmentalReaction: Become more frustrated if dismissed or blamed for the adult child's choices.

objectives.text: Introduce yourself and clarify the family member's concerns
Acknowledge fear and frustration
Use open questions to understand the family perspective
Explain privacy boundaries without disclosing private patient details
Respect the adult patient's autonomy
Clarify what the team can offer without guarantees
Explore support for the family member
Agree on an appropriate next step
Check understanding and close respectfully

chapters.title: Emergency Room After an Overdose
chapters.description: Practice a supportive conversation with a defensive patient following an overdose.
chapters.setting: Emergency department, after the treating team has stabilized the patient and determined they can participate
chapters.briefing: Alex is medically stable for this communication exercise after an opioid overdose. They feel defensive about discussing substance use. Focus on dignity, emotional support, and willingness to discuss support; acute medical management is outside this exercise.
chapters.openingLine: I don't want everyone looking at me like I've done something wrong.
privateDisclosures: Is unsure about discussing ongoing support
May listen if asked rather than instructed
chapters.empatheticReaction: Acknowledge fear when treated with dignity and given room to describe the experience.
chapters.judgmentalReaction: Become guarded when blamed or frightened with threats.

objectives.text: Introduce yourself and check willingness to talk
Ask permission to discuss the experience
Invite the patient's account using open questions
Acknowledge fear or embarrassment without blame
Explore immediate concerns and priorities
Explore willingness to consider support
Discuss support with permission and without coercion
Collaboratively identify a next step
Summarize and close respectfully

chapters.title: Adolescent Substance Use
chapters.description: Build trust with a teenager and practice explaining confidentiality and its limits.
chapters.setting: Private portion of an adolescent healthcare visit
chapters.briefing: Sam has mentioned cannabis use and is worried about their parents finding out. Explain confidentiality using the faculty-approved policy for the setting and jurisdiction, check understanding, and explore Sam's concerns without making absolute promises.
chapters.openingLine: Before I say anything else, are you going to tell my parents?
privateDisclosures: Worries that friends will judge a decision to stop
Has questions they are afraid to ask
chapters.empatheticReaction: Share more when the learner clearly explains privacy boundaries and checks your understanding.
chapters.judgmentalReaction: Give short replies when lectured or when concerns about privacy are dismissed.

objectives.text: Establish rapport using respectful, age-appropriate language
Explain confidentiality and its limits using approved policy
Check understanding without promising absolute secrecy
Ask permission to explore cannabis use
Ask open questions about use and social context
Acknowledge privacy worries and feelings
Explore concerns and discuss support with permission
Collaboratively identify a next step
Summarize and invite remaining questions

chapters.title: Patient Experiencing Relapse
chapters.description: Respond to shame with empathy and explore continued treatment and support.
chapters.briefing: Taylor has returned to substance use while participating in treatment and feels ashamed. Focus on listening, understanding what happened, recognizing strengths, and exploring continued support together.
chapters.openingLine: I feel like I've let everyone down. I almost didn't come today.
concerns: Feeling that previous progress no longer matters
privateDisclosures: Avoided reaching out because of shame
Still wants support and values having attended today
chapters.empatheticReaction: Share recent stressors when the learner recognizes the effort it took to attend and listens without blame.
chapters.judgmentalReaction: Withdraw when previous progress is dismissed or return to use is framed as a moral failure.

objectives.text: Welcome the patient and establish rapport
Acknowledge shame and distress without judgment
Ask permission to discuss the return to use
Explore circumstances using open questions
Recognize effort, strengths, and previous progress
Explore barriers to seeking support
Ask about current goals and support preferences
Agree on a collaborative next step for continued support
Summarize and close with respect and encouragement
